body:
What is electronic mail?

Electronic mail, usually written as e-mail or email, is a service for exchanging digital messages through computer networks. It allows a sender to prepare a message and address it to one or more recipients. A message can contain written information and may include attached files.

E-mail is not the same as a web page. Both may use the Internet, but e-mail uses its own message-delivery arrangements. A person can also use e-mail through a website called webmail, where a browser provides access to the mailbox.

Understanding an e-mail address

Consider the illustrative address student@example.org.

The part before the @ symbol, student, is the local part of the address. The part after it, example.org, is the domain part. Together they identify an electronic mailbox address.

The domain part helps the mail system determine where the message should be delivered. An e-mail address is different from a website URL: an address such as student@example.org identifies a mailbox, whereas a web URL identifies a web resource.

Essential fields of an e-mail message

An e-mail message commonly contains information identifying the sender, the recipients and the message content.

Field or elementPurpose
FromDisplays the sender's address
ToIdentifies the primary recipients
CcCarbon copy; includes additional recipients whose addresses are ordinarily visible to other recipients
BccBlind carbon copy; includes recipients without revealing their addresses to the other recipients
SubjectProvides a brief description of the message topic
BodyContains the main message
AttachmentAn additional file sent with the message, such as a document or photograph

The Subject is not the main message; the Body contains the actual communication. An attachment is a separate file associated with the message. Depending on the mail service, attachments may be subject to size or type restrictions.

Difference between To, Cc and Bcc

Suppose an office sends an official circular to an employee and wants the section head to receive a copy. The employee may be entered in To and the section head in Cc. Both addresses are ordinarily visible to the recipients.

When the same notice must be sent to a large number of people without showing each person's address to the others, Bcc may be used. Bcc conceals recipient addresses from the other recipients, but it is not a guarantee of complete secrecy for the message itself.

To identifies primary recipients; Cc sends a visible copy; Bcc sends a copy without displaying those recipient addresses to other recipients.

How an e-mail reaches the recipient

After the sender submits a message, an outgoing mail service arranges its delivery. The message may pass between mail servers before reaching the recipient's mailbox. The recipient can then access that mailbox through an e-mail application or a webmail service.

SMTP, or Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, is the standard protocol associated with sending and relaying electronic mail. It is not primarily the protocol used to read messages already stored in a mailbox.

Two other abbreviations are useful for distinguishing message retrieval from message sending:

  • IMAP: Internet Message Access Protocol. It allows an e-mail client to access and manage messages stored on a mail server, supporting synchronization across devices.
  • POP3: Post Office Protocol version 3. It is used to retrieve messages from a mail server, commonly by downloading them to an e-mail client. Whether messages remain on the server depends on the client's settings and service behavior.

For example, a person may compose an e-mail through a webmail page accessed using HTTPS. The browser-based interface does not change the underlying distinction: SMTP is used in the sending and transport of e-mail, while mailbox-access mechanisms allow the recipient to view received messages.

Practical precautions

A file attachment should be opened carefully when its sender or purpose is uncertain. Also, the address shown in the From field is not by itself conclusive proof of the sender's identity. These precautions are especially relevant when e-mail carries forms, official notices or personal documents.

Prelims focus

  • An e-mail address contains a local part, the @ symbol and a domain part.
  • Cc: Carbon copy; recipients are ordinarily visible.
  • Bcc: Blind carbon copy; addresses are concealed from the other recipients.
  • SMTP: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol; sends and relays e-mail.
  • IMAP and POP3 are associated with accessing or retrieving received messages.
  • Trap: SMTP is not the principal protocol for reading received e-mail.

[NCERT, Class 12, India: People and Economy, Chapter 10, Transport and Communication, p. 123, section Personal Communication System; Mozilla Thunderbird Help, Addressing an Email, section Address Fields: To, Cc, Bcc, consulted 15 November 2026; IETF, RFC 5321, Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, Sections 1.1 and 2; Cloudflare Learning Center, What Is SMTP?, section SMTP vs. IMAP and POP, consulted 15 November 2026.]

body:
Meaning of cloud computing

Cloud computing is a way of providing computing resources and services through a network, commonly the Internet. Instead of relying only on files and software stored on a user's own device, a person or organization can access storage, applications and other resources supplied by a remote service provider.

For example, a learner may store notes in an online account and later access the same notes from a different device. Similarly, an office may use a web-based service to work on shared documents without installing all the service's components on every computer.

Cloud computing provides convenient, on-demand network access to computing resources such as storage, applications and services.

Local storage and cloud storage

When a document is saved only on a local computer, access ordinarily depends on that computer or a copy of the file. When it is stored through a cloud storage service, an authorized user may be able to access it from several connected devices.

This difference does not mean that every cloud document is always available. Access may depend on Internet connectivity, the user's account, service availability and permissions. Some cloud applications provide offline access to previously downloaded copies, but this varies by service.

Main characteristics of cloud services

Cloud computing commonly provides resources when users need them, makes services available through network connections and allows providers to share resources among many users while managing access appropriately.

Important features include:

  • On-demand self-service: Users can obtain supported resources automatically when required, without human interaction with the service provider.
  • Broad network access: Services can be reached through supported devices over a network.
  • Resource pooling: A provider can serve multiple users from managed computing resources.
  • Rapid elasticity: Available resources can be increased or reduced according to demand.
  • Measured service: Resource use can be monitored and measured.

These characteristics describe the cloud-computing model. They do not imply that every individual cloud service is free, unlimited or suitable for every purpose.

Common cloud service models

Three important abbreviations classify cloud services according to the type of resource supplied.

ModelFull formWhat the customer mainly receives
SaaSSoftware as a ServiceA ready-to-use application, such as online e-mail or document editing
PaaSPlatform as a ServiceA managed environment for running applications
IaaSInfrastructure as a ServiceBasic computing resources such as processing capacity and storage

The distinction is what the provider supplies. With SaaS, users mainly work with a finished application. PaaS provides a managed environment for applications. IaaS provides underlying computing resources that the customer can configure and use.

Public, private and hybrid clouds

Cloud services can also be classified by their deployment arrangement:

  • Public cloud: Cloud services offered for open use by the general public through a provider.
  • Private cloud: Cloud infrastructure made available for exclusive use by one organization.
  • Hybrid cloud: An arrangement combining 2 or more distinct cloud infrastructures that remain separate but are connected to enable data or application portability.

The word public in public cloud does not mean that every customer's documents are publicly readable. Access to information still depends on service permissions and security arrangements.

Benefits and limitations

Cloud services can make remote access, collaboration and resource expansion easier. They may reduce the need for an organization to maintain every service entirely on its own premises. However, users must still consider account security, privacy, service interruptions, costs and the availability of important documents.

Cloud synchronization is not necessarily a separate backup. If an unwanted deletion or alteration is synchronized across devices, the change may also appear in the cloud copy. Important files may therefore require an independent backup or suitable recovery arrangements.

How the major Internet terms fit together

The main concepts of this subtopic describe different parts of a connected digital system:

  • LAN, MAN and WAN classify networks according to geographical extent.
  • Internet refers to the worldwide interconnection of networks; WWW refers to linked web resources accessed through it.
  • IP provides network addressing; DNS helps resolve domain names into addresses.
  • URL identifies a resource and its access scheme; a browser opens web resources using protocols such as HTTP or HTTPS.
  • SMTP handles e-mail sending and transport; FTP is associated with transferring files.
  • Cloud computing provides remotely accessible computing resources and services over a network.

These relationships are important because a single practical activity may involve several concepts at once. For example, opening an online document may involve a LAN or another access network, Internet connectivity, DNS resolution, a web URL, HTTPS communication and a cloud-based application. Each term describes a different part of the activity rather than a competing name for the whole process.

Prelims focus

  • Cloud computing: On-demand network access to computing resources and services.
  • SaaS: Software as a Service; ready-to-use applications.
  • PaaS: Platform as a Service; managed application environment.
  • IaaS: Infrastructure as a Service; basic computing resources.
  • Public, private and hybrid are cloud deployment arrangements.
  • Trap: Cloud storage is not automatically an independent backup, and cloud computing is not another name for the Internet.

[National Institute of Standards and Technology, The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing, Special Publication 800-145, September 2011, definition, essential characteristics, service models and deployment models; NIST Cloud Computing Program, program description, consulted 15 November 2026; ICANN, The Domain Name System, DNS overview, consulted 15 November 2026; MDN Web Docs, What is a URL? and HTTPS, introductory explanations, consulted 15 November 2026; IETF, RFC 5321, Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, Section 1.1; IETF, RFC 959, File Transfer Protocol, Section 1.]
